questions.solution: The given idiomatic expression 'Out for the count' means 'unconscious or soundly asleep' (In a deep, insensible sleep). ​Ex: It looks like Ben's out for the count.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. An eye wash
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution: The given idiomatic expression 'An eye wash' means misleading or deceptive statements, actions, or procedures; 'A pretence'. Example: She says she'll quit her job, but we know that's just an eyewash.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Go bonkers
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Go bonkers
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is Become crazy.

Key Points

  • Let's look at the meaning of the given idiom:-
  • Go bonkers -  To be or become wild, restless, irrational, or crazy or to act in such a way. (जंगली, बेचैन, तर्कहीन या पागल होना या इस तरह से कार्य करना)
    • For Example - Don't give the kids too much sugar or they'll end up going bonkers!

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pull someone up
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Pull someone up
questions.solution: To pull someone up means to criticize or reprimand them for something they have done wrong. For example, the boss pulled him up for being late to work again.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Over the moon
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Over the moon
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Extremely happy'

  • Let's see an example-
    • She was over the moon about/with her new bike.
  • Hence, the correct answer is Option 2.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Babe in the woods
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Babe in the woods
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'A young defenceless person'
Key Points
  • The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom 'Babe in the woods​​' is 'A young defenceless person'.
  • Let’s look at the meaning and example of the given phrasal verb:

      • E.g. When I began my political career, I was a mere babe in the woods.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cup of tea
questions.questionHtml:

Cup of tea
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 2.
Key Points 

  • 'Cup of tea' is an expression that is used to describe something you like, something you are good at or something you enjoy doing. (अपनी पसंद की किसी चीज़ का वर्णन करने के लिए, जिस चीज़ में आप अच्छे हैं या जिसे करने में आपको मज़ा आता है)

options.html: To run about in a frenzy

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To be off your food
questions.questionHtml:

To be off your food
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'To have no appetite'.

Key Points

  • The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom 'To be off your food' is 'To have no appetite'.
  • To be off your food: not wanting to eat, usually because you are ill. (खाने का मन नहीं, आमतौर पर क्योंकि आप बीमार हैं)
    • Example: It's not like you to be off your food.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Comb through

questions.question: Select the meaning of the given idiom. Be at your wits' end
questions.questionHtml:
Select the meaning of the given idiom.

Be at your wits' end
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.
Key Points

  • So,  the meaning of the given idiom 'Be at your wits' end' is 'Be overwhelmed with problems'.

questions.question: Select the meaning of the given idiom. All and sundry
questions.questionHtml:
Select the meaning of the given idiom.

All and sundry
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 3.

 All and sundry means everyone.

So, the meaning of the given idiom is 'All included'.
Example: I made tea for all and sundry at the office.

questions.question: Select the meaning of the given idiom. Chip off the old block
questions.questionHtml:
Select the meaning of the given idiom.

Chip off the old block
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 3.

'Chip off the old block' means someone whose character or personality resembles that of their parent.

Example: Mike's automotive repair skills really rival those of his father. He's a real chip off the old block!

questions.question: Select the meaning of the given idiom. To pour oil in troubled water
questions.questionHtml:
Select the meaning of the given idiom.

To pour oil in troubled water
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

Key Points

  • 'To pour oil in troubled water' means to calm or settle a tense situation.
  • So, the meaning of the given idiom is to calm a dispute.
  • Example: If those two are arguing again, send Mom in to talk to them—she's great at pouring oil on troubled waters.

​ Confusion Points

  • Many of us will get confused that option 2 or 4 is the correct answer. But the correct answer is- to settle a disagreement or dispute with words intended to placate or pacify those involved. Hence, the given answer is correct.

questions.question: Select the meaning of the given idiom. Fair's fair

So, the meaning of the given idiom is 'Just treatment'.

Example: You may not like her, but fair's fair, she's a good teacher.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hit the ceiling

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Months on end

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. The eldest prince was declared the heir of a throne .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

The eldest prince was declared the heir of a throne.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'heir to the throne'

Key Points

  • The word heir means someone who inherits the position of a King/Queen/ancestors and their assets or properties.
  •  Heir is a noun. The heir is always used with the heir to something or heir of someone.
  • Here the use of infinitive to as a verb demonstrates purpose. Meaning to take over as king/queen.

Hence, the correct sentence is: The eldest prince was declared the heir to the throne.

Additional Information

  • When we say heir of someone. We mean heir of a person, or family but not a position or role.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase. Now and again
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase. 

Now and again
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Occasionally.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Now and again" means something that happens occasionally or from time to time. (कभी-कभी)
    • Example: Now and again, she likes to take a walk in the park to clear her mind.
  • "Occasionally" refers to something that happens infrequently or at irregular intervals. (कभी-कभी)
    • Example: I only see my cousins occasionally, usually during holidays.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Occasionally.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Always (हमेशा): At all times; on all occasions.
    • Example: She always takes her coffee with sugar.
  • To be continued (जारी रहेगा): Something that will be continued at a later time.
    • Example: The story was left on a cliffhanger, to be continued in the next episode.
  • At present time or future (वर्तमान समय या भविष्य में): Refers to something happening now or in the future.
    • Example: We are currently working on the project, and it will be completed in the near future.

Yeoman service
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e., Useful help in need.

Key Points

Let's look at the following points-

  •  The phrase Yeoman's service/work means efficient or useful help in need.
  •  Example: The army has done Yeoman's service during natural disasters.
  •  The phrase has originated from the word 'Yeoman', which meant an honest, hardworking man working in noble households/ cultivating a small agricultural land.  

Thus, the correct option is 3 and therefore the answer.
